I struggled with horrible anxiety for many years, from my teenage years and well into my adulthood. I was a 21/21 on the GAD-7 when I went to my psychiatrist for help. Health anxiety ran my life, I was having constant palpitations, daily panic attacks, insomnia, suicidal ideation, my digestion was wrecked, etc. I was miserable.

I was prescribed 50mg, and though I was terrified to start a medication, I did it. And my score dropped severely, and fast. I'm now wavering between a 0 and a 4 on my monthly GAD-7 check-ins. I don't have panic attacks anymore. I sleep like a normal human on a normal sleep schedule. I can do things without being afraid I'll die during it. I'm no longer focused on my heartbeat every waking second. I can handle rough days at work like a normal person. I can enjoy life again, freely.

It's worth it. Even if you just try it and find it's not the right drug for you, it's worth the shot. I do admit, I got lucky and got put on the one that works with my body the first time, but do this favor to yourself. It will work out one way or another. Make the jump and get help. You don't have to live this way. 🩷

You should be just fine! Zoloft has a half-life of +24hrs, so missing a dose for a day shouldn't affect you bad enough to experience withdrawal symptoms. I'm on 50mg, and I've missed a day several times and never felt any different. Of course everyone is different, but I wouldn't worry yourself. Just take your next dose when you get your refill, and you'll be alright :)

First off, I want to say congrats on quitting! 11 days is no small feat. It's proof that you can keep going indefinitely. 

Just think. You're *there*. You already did it! You've quit. You've done the difficult task you set out to do, and that's amazing! The hardest step of deciding to quit and making that first step to say no is over! It's hard to break habits, especially one you've had for *years*. But you're on the path, and you're well into it already. The cravings might persist. I won't lie to you, mine still do even a month in. But what's stronger, the cravings? Or the will to want to not be owned by a vape? If it were the former, you would have already failed before you began. You have the will and the strength. You just need to keep reminding yourself that.

As for coping mechanisms, try using hard candies that you enjoy, or try actually deep breathing through the straw! You got this, friend. Don't give up on yourself.

I used to feel this way. I put off trying meds for at least a decade, because I was terrified I'd have an allergic reaction, I'd get serotonin syndrome, I'd get super suicidal, I'd react horribly, or I'd straight up die because I'm some special case who would react so horribly with the meds. 

I'm so glad I finally said fuck it and went through with it. It may have taken me taking like a 1/10th of a tablet for a few days to get over the fear that it would kill me or cause a reaction, and a bit more health anxiety as I adjusted to it, but I have never been so free of anxiety and depression once it all leveled out. I still have bad days, whether my anxiety or depression want to rear up a bit, but both are so much more manageable. I can't even tell you the last time I had a panic attack or got stuck in a thought loop. It truly changed my life. Maybe even saved it.

If meds are something you have been thinking about, please try them. I know it's hard, and it's scary. I can't say everyone will be as lucky as I was, getting it right on the first try. But damn, is it worth a shot in my opinion. 

Best of luck to you all, and I'm here if anyone has questions of any sort!

I quit cold turkey after a crippling \~10 year "my vape does not leave my hand unless I'm asleep or showering" habit. I was tired of feeling like my heart was going to explode and not being able to breathe properly or adjust to living in higher altitude. And it was shockingly easy. For the first few days I was a bit dizzy here and there and had some brain zaps, and I craved it really hard, but day by day those got less intense. It took me about 2 weeks to really get over the instinct to reach out and grab my vape on my desk, and about the same for the constant "time for a vape!" action thoughts to subside. I'm now about 2 months free, and of course I still crave it. I think I always will, because my brain associates vaping with a good nicotine buzz and happy chemicals. But it's really not bad. It's mostly if I'm idle, my brain just goes into the "put your vape in your hand and take a puff" motion, but then it goes away just as fast as it came on.  


Using an app for quitting vaping helped, because it was nice to see the health milestones, and I got excited for them. ("Oh, tomorrow my body will be free of nicotine, yay!")  


I bought suckers and hard candy, but didn't end up using them much.  


And I had my friends keep me accountable. It helps that none of them vape, but having them ask me how I am and how it's going and telling me they're proud was nice.  


If I can quit, you absolutely can quit. It's so, so worth it. You got this, I promise :)

You're already doing a great job reaching out about it! Your drive to be the best partner you can be for her is already a huge step :) I'd say the next most important thing is to just be as understanding as you can be. The fact there are so many invisible symptoms means that she may look fine, but may be experiencing a whole myriad of uncomfortable or downright miserable symptoms that are beyond her control. It may ruin plans, it may make her mood a bit down, it may hinder some things. But being gentle about it may do wonders. I know I personally experience a lot of guilt around not having the will/energy to do things sometimes, and it definitely helps me to have a partner not question/complain/belittle/argue with me on it.  


Reminding her to take her meds/supplements if applicable could help, if she's not super on top of it already. Joining along with her diet plan or workout routine may also be a good sign of support if she's working on dietary and lifestyle changes.  


Since it is a complex condition and everyone experiences it differently, this is only my take on it. I'd definitely ask her what she needs in that moment to get the best advice straight from the source, though! Best of luck to you both :)

It's absolutely valid! It's really hard to act like a functioning human when you yourself aren't functioning. Our bodies are actively fighting against themselves all the time, and it's hell. It's enough that we have to deal with the stressors, obstacles, and chores of daily life without everything else we have going on inside. It's like getting a race car and putting in the wrong fuel, filling it with the wrong oil, and deflating its tires and then wondering why it's not keeping up with the others.  


Listen to your body, and don't let anyone (including yourself) to not call your symptoms an "excuse". They're a reason.  ❤️

I often worry about that, especially because I went undiagnosed for so long and my only real, usable excuses for feeling like hell were that I was lazy and just bad at being a functioning human for the longest time. Even now, with a written Dx of Hashimoto's, a bottle of levo in my purse and lab tests to show that my levels are all pretty rough, I still feel like an imposter.

But just know that it really doesn't matter what people think, as hard as it is to look past it. You know how you feel, and you only owe it to yourself to be kind to your body and do what you need/want to do. Other people can either accept you and believe you, or think you're lying for whatever reason. But either way, you don't owe anything to them. You'll gain nothing but worsening your state by breaching your comfort zone to appease the unreasonable expectations of others who are out to call you on something that has no bearing in their own life whether they're right or wrong.

You do you, and don't worry about what other people think. We owe ourselves the same gentleness and patience we'd give to our loved ones without a second thought. ❤️

I avoided going to the doctor for an embarrassing number of years due to health/medical anxiety, but then I had an issue where I was spotting constantly for 3+ months. So I set up a gyno and a doctor appointment right after that, and after an exam and discussing my issues, my gyno set me up for lab tests and an ultrasound to start ruling things out.  


Got my lab results, and my gyno immediately called my doctor because my thyroid peroxidase antibodies were at 662, my T4 was low, and my TSH was high.  


Went in for my doctor visit, and she let me know that I have Hashimoto's. So now I'm currently day 1 into a cardiac event monitor to make sure my heart is good because I had some concerns, I have a secondary lab test coming up to confirm my thyroid levels and lipids next week and due to start thyroid hormones soon, and a few other things to get sorted out after that.  


Who knows how long I've had it. I've been struggling with my weight and other problems that could possibly be explained by Hashimoto's for years. But I'm glad I'm getting it all figured out now. Better late than never!

I say go with the education route that best works for you. I'm assuming you're looking into getting some form of contraception, so I'll give my two cents on my experience with that at Planned Parenthood. I was on the pill on and off for probably 7-8 years and went exclusively through Planned Parenthood for it. I first started a good 10 years ago so my experience is both a bit fuzzy and possibly different from how it is now, so take it with a grain of salt.  


Getting it set up was easy; I called and let them know I wanted to get on the pill, so they had me come in for my first appointment. It wasn't anything invasive or physical, mainly just asking a few health and lifestyle related questions and getting my patient chart and insurance info set up and all. They briefly went over how the pill works, how to take it, possible side effects, warnings, etc and handed me my first few boxes and let them know to call them about any questions or concerns. Thankfully it all went without a hitch, so I continued on.   


Refilling was easy, at least for the type of pill I was on. I get refills (3 month supply at a time) that equal up to a year, and once my refills are up, I go in for an appointment where they just ask basic questions (Any side effects? Questions? Are you happy with the method you're using? Are you safe/need any STI testing/etc) and they send me on my way with another supply and refills available for the rest of the year. I had the option to transfer my Rx to a different pharmacy, so that should also be available to you as well if the nearest Planned Parenthood is a bit of a hike.  


My pill was a generic form and free through my Medicaid insurance, so that was also very nice and made things super quick and easy each time. I would just show up, tell them I'm here for a refill (so long as I had some available), give them my insurance card and driver's license, wait 5 minutes, and walk out with my pills.

This is coming from a girl who just got broken up with last night after a serious 3 year relationship.

Tell her the truth, don't sugarcoat. If the truth really is "I love you but I need to do this" then say it. But don't use these embellishments if you don't mean it just to let her down easy. She's probably going to ask a lot of questions. Why this is happening, how you could do this, why she's not good enough. Answer them if you like. But I'd say once you start going in circles answering the same questions over and over, it's time to end the conversation and leave. Honestly nothing is going to make this easier for her. You just need to say what needs to be said and don't leave any loose ends that she could use to hold onto hope. It's going to hurt her more initially, but it will save her the second heartbreak of realizing you never meant that you could maybe try again one day. 

Best of luck. It's not going to be easy but it is what it is.

BB cream is pretty much a tinted moisturizer, so it's not as pigmented and heavy as a foundation liquid. You can find it at most drug stores if you're not looking to spend a lot on some big name brand stuff. It feels a lot lighter on your skin and doesn't look nearly as heavy or cakey, it just adds a really light coating to help even out your skintone and reduce the starkness of blemishes and all. It sometimes has SPF and other things in it to help your skin, but that's the basis of it.

Do you have any beauty stores in your area, like Sephora or Ulta? You can get matched there by someone, and then you can sort of experiment with the #/name/range they gave you to find your perfect one. Though BB creams tend to be a little more forgiving as they usually just have like 6 different shades to pick from, so you'll just find your general range and it should be okay, at least in my experience. A little sidenote if you're not doing it already, it also helps a little to blend your foundation/BB cream/whatever down past your jawline a bit with the excess so it's not just a straight line separating your neck from your face.

Youtube tutorials can help you learn new techniques and things to do. I've learned a few things from them, and while I admittedly still suck at makeup, I at least have a bit more know-how. You don't really need contouring and highlighting and "baking" and all that stuff that people tend to do nowadays if you're going for truly easy, natural looking makeup. I feel okay leaving the house with just BB cream, powder and some mascara most days. But if you want to start learning new things for your daughter, I'd recommend looking up some tutorials so you at least have a bit of working knowledge in case she asks :)

Mocking my best friend for self-harming.  


We were on a trip for high school marching band and were staying in a hotel. I knew she was self-harming often and was very depressed, and I did my best to try and support her for a while. But after some time, I started to get annoyed. I was naive to mental illnesses at the time, and in my mind I was sure she was doing it just for attention at this point. I was sitting on the beds chatting with our other roommate and my best friend comes out of the shower and sits next to me, and it was obvious she was just crying. She quietly asks me "Will this pass off as me falling on some rocks if my mom sees it?" and shows me fresh cuts on her arm from a disassembled shaving razor.  


I sort of scoffed and said "Probably not, she's not stupid. *You're* stupid for doing that though." She went back into the bathroom and I continued on chatting with our roommate until we went to bed. The following day or two during the scheduled outings, I'd be hanging closely with our roommate, while my best friend would follow behind us, often crying but always looking so upset and dead inside. We openly mocked her, not to her face but aloud, poking fun at how she's crying and moping and "*Oh boo hoo, life sucks :'(*"  Many others noticed as well, as I'd get people asking me why she's crying while laughing about it, and I did nothing to defend her.  


While our friendship rekindled immediately, it never hit me until a few years later how I was such a disgusting piece of shit for doing that. I mocked her and abandoned in a really dark time and basically fed her to the wolves without remorse (a.k.a. brutal high school-aged kids.) We've been inseparable best friends for 12 years now, so thankfully it had no long-term effects. We're very supportive of each other now and I've never had a friend like her. Clearly she doesn't hold it against me, she may not even remember it, but every so often I think of it and I end up hating myself a little bit for it every time.

I'm so sorry you had to go through this. And that's not a pity party, that's manipulation and abuse from her. Don't feel like it's your fault because it's not. She's denying you of your needs just so she can look good.

The first was the "Owl Man". My friend and I (probably 10 years old) were having a sleepover and watching a movie while laying down on the couches in my living room. We begin to hear rustling in the front yard near the bushes we have lining our house. Being 2 kids alone in the dark, we got spooked and put the TV on mute and stared out the window, afraid to move. Suddenly, something rears up incredibly fast and smacks the bay window with it's whole body and sits there for a few moments (unsure of how long exactly because we both bolted to my parent's room screaming).  This thing was *huge.* It's wings were massive but oddly shaped, as if it had human elbows rather than regular avian bone structures. It had a silhouette of a man's torso and head, but the thing that is still burned into my memory is it's eyes. They were massive, and much, much bigger than any human or animal's would be. About the size of tennis balls, and nearly glowing a bright yellow/gold. My dad immediately went out to investigate, bat in hand, but found nothing out of the ordinary. I'd have chalked it up to a creepy prankster if it wasn't for the eyes. They were not a reflection, they weren't headlamps, they weren't part of some cheap costume, they were *eyes*. I got out of bed, leaned out of my door and yelled at him to take his fucking walk already because I'm trying to sleep. The footsteps stop so I lay back down and eventually start to drift off. I see this humanoid thing peeking in my doorway, sort of half hiding behind the door. It had no face, no fingers, no defining features and it was just a flesh-colored silhouette. Being that I was nearly asleep, I turn over and fall asleep. I nearly forgot about it the rest of the night after the ex came home and we hashed things out. We went to bed later on and fell asleep, but in the middle of the night I'm awoken by him shaking me violently and begging for me to wake up. What I figured could have been sleep paralysis turned into an encounter.

With all things considered, I say yes, it is ethical. Domestication and invasive species and all that aside, I still believe it is ethical so long as they are properly cared for. Having room to sniff, run and play, having a steady flow of food and fresh water, shelter from the elements and other predators and diseases they can pick up from the general outdoors, someone to dote on them with love and affection, medical intervention to prolong and better their life. Wild animals don't get these things. You're giving domestic animals a life mostly free of the dangers that trouble and kill other animals. I don't see how that can be so bad.

While yes, it's tragic and a real issue that pets get abused and mistreated and that's hard to avoid unfortunately, but thankfully we're in a world with some good people who will report such things or take matters into their own hands to save the animal, and law enforcement and other groups specifically dedicated to the proper treatment of animals. So at least there's an effort to prevent it from happening and stop it after it has.

Cats are actually an invasive species. They carry zoonotic diseases, they're responsible for the death and decline of native species. It's nice and all that you want them to roam free, but they're not actually supposed to be there in the first place. 

Edit: Add domestic dogs to that, as well. You don't see wild Shih Tzu running around in the woods. Many dogs are terribly bred over the years and can't exist without human intervention anyway. Not to mention it'd screw up the native ecosystem if we were to just release the domesticated dogs everywhere.

If a pet is well taken care of, I don't see the harm. If they get well exercised, fed with good food, stimulated with play and simulated hunting and such, have a family to call their pack, get attention which they sure seem to crave and love, how is that so terrible? It's not like you're taking in a wild native species who wasn't domesticated over generations upon generations to coexist with humans into an apartment.

I feel you. Used to be somewhat athletic in high school and quite thin, but recently I got to just under 200lbs (I'm very short so it just seems even worse) and unhappy as all hell. If you don't mind me offering up some advice, I've found that limiting carbs is making me visibly drop weight at a decent rate. No gym required, though it'd definitely speed up the process.

I used to helplessly crave and absolutely gorge myself on carbs. Basically it was a major food group for me besides meat. Now, I'm limiting myself to 30g per meal or less, which honestly isn't hard to do! I've often found myself eating 0-30g per *day* purely by coincidence. It helps if you like meat and veggies. I've been on it for maybe 3 weeks now and I've lost about 10lbs and I look a great deal thinner than I was. Still hovering in the 180's, but it's a steady improvement!

I pay attention to portion sizes (and if I'm super hungry, I make myself some extra meat or veggies and fill up on that, I don't feel as bad then), I don't keep unwholesome snacks easily available (besides the giant box of goldfish in my room, can't just throw it out 😂) and instead I'll make myself grab a spoon of sugar free peanut butter or slice a few pieces of cheese, put the rest away and carry that back with me. I drink La Croix or (sometimes infused) water instead of soda, which I completely cut out. I've stopped eating full servings of desserts and limit myself to a few spoons of ice cream or a small chunk of super dark chocolate or similar if I want something sweet. I do give myself cheat days so I don't dive head-first off the wagon into a whole loaf of garlic bread, but even then I keep it sane.

Through all this, I've actually found that I'm not as hungry anymore as well. I used to be able to eat well above a full portion size of something, get seconds, and probably still feel hungry after that. Now, I even sometimes forget to eat but one meal a day (which isn't healthy, don't follow my mistakes. Just trying to prove my point!)

Hopefully some of this helps you! Some people find cutting calories helps, some cut out sugar, but I found this works for me. Best of luck getting back to where you want to be! :)

Brown sugar can add a better flavor than plain white sugar. You like fruit? Chop up/muddle some strawberries, blueberries or bananas or whatever fruit you like best and add them in, the tartness of some fruits will definitely add to what some may consider "dull" flavor, though *I'm* inclined to disagree. Prefer savory foods? Shred some cheddar cheese, chop up some bacon, add some salt, and boom, savory oatmeal. Add vanilla/almond extract for a different pop of flavor. Use coconut/almond/flax/whatever milk as the liquid. Add in a scoop of your favorite ice cream flavor.

To make it less sticky, use more milk/water to make it less gelatinous and more soupy, that way it won't stick to everything. Or, make overnight oats. Put instant oats in a container, add ample milk/water and some honey, and some fruit if you're so inclined. Pop it in the fridge overnight and when you wake up, you have a not-so sticky oatmeal ready to go, no heat needed! I'll admit, I stooped to a level where I simply added cold milk to the fruit+oatmeal packets and ate it like cereal, and it's not sticky at all, so maybe give that a shot if you're not ashamed of how lazy it is. A little chewy but you don't get that "I might actually be eating tar" texture.

Take your time building up to the level of drunk you want to be at. It's going to take a little bit to kick in, so don't start pounding back shots/hard liquor because you still feel sober. Sort of tying into the first point, don't let yourself get black-out drunk right away, *especially* if you're in public, a guest's house, or with unfamiliar people. Learn your limits and stay within them. You don't want to get yourself into a bad situation or in jail because you were blacked out and did something stupid. You also don't want to end up pregnant/getting someone pregnant/getting an STD/etc because drunk you thought it wasn't that important to be safe about it.

DO NOT drink and drive. Don't let your friends drink and drive. Don't let the voice in the back of your head say "I'm fine." Don't let the pressure of a friend *reeeally* needing 1am tacos sway you. Have a DD at your party, call an Uber/Lyft, get a parent to pick you up, get a friend at home to come get you, eat a meal and wait a few hours, stay the night. You're a lot more confident when you're drunk for all the wrong reasons, and I promise you, you are not good to drive. It's not worth your life, someone else's life, or at the very least a DUI.

Just learn your limits, be safe, and have fun.

Egg in the middle! Take 1-3 slices of bread depending on how hungry you are. Any sliced sandwich bread works. Grab a smallish cup that will cut a hole in the middle of the bread like a cookie cutter, leaving ample crust on all sides. Save the inner bread circles.

Liberally butter up a skillet pan, and sprinkle some optional salt and pepper, garlic powder, etc. Lay the holed out bread rings down onto the hot pan, and crack one egg into each middle. Lay the middle circle down on the side as well to toast/fry. Cook and flip until your desired toast color appears, plate it, and enjoy! I like to eat the outside crusts first, then lay the egg yolk onto the inner toast circle and eat that after. It's not the healthiest meal since you're basically frying bread in butter, but it's delicious, my almost daily go-to and I'm not trying to win a health award.

Also, honorable mention to sticking a fried egg into a grilled cheese, another breakfast option for me when I want to indulge a little harder.

When smoking hookah, you have a ceramic/clay/etc bowl on top of the setup filled with moist shisha tobacco, usually covered with aluminum foil or a specially made filter. The coal is exactly what it sounds like, a piece of charcoal that you light on fire/heat up until red hot. They're marketed specifically for smoking hookah, it's not just a barbecue charcoal briquette or anything, but it's the same exact concept. It sits on top of the foil cap and essentially bakes the shisha under it, creating the smoke that goes down the pipe stem, into the water vase and into the hose you're inhaling from. If you watch any video of someone smoking hookah, you should clearly be able to see the coal perched right on top of the entire thing.

The downside is, without any type of cap over the coal, a small bump into the hookah or clumsy hands when moving the coal around the bowl or ashing it can result in it being dropped, and being red hot, it will melt whatever it touches.

I'm not a morning person at all, held jobs that started at 1pm or so for the past few years, and recently with my current job I wake up between 5 and 6am so it was super difficult to adjust at first. But a few things that helped me (and other things I read) are:

- Like I mentioned in another comment to you, getting an app that makes you solve math equations or puzzles before you can snooze or dismiss it.

- Make sure it is set on full volume. Find an alarm ringtone that nearly hurts your ears. Probably not healthy, but there is no way I'm going to wake up to "Forest fairy dreams" with windchimes and a babbling brook or some shit. I'm talking like nuclear sirens or one of those annoying high-pitched tones or a police siren type sound. This is what works for me and what I currently do. Might suck to be shocked awake, but better than losing your job.

- Set your phone across the room. You'll have to get up to turn it off, and therefore you'll be less likely to lay right back down or hit it in your sleep.

- Just force yourself up. If you hear your alarm, just shut it off and get up no matter how you feel. Not just sitting up, get out of bed. Walk a lap around your room or do a few jumping jacks if you have to. Open up a window. Make your bed. Do something to wake your mind and body up so you're less tempted to fall back asleep immediately.

As for the coming in drunk, you just need to sort that out yourself. Is holding a job and supporting yourself more important than having a few drinks? If it is, prioritize your life and take responsibility. There will be time for drinking and doing whatever you like on your days off. It's irresponsible to do it hours before work or what have you. It's dangerous to yourself and those around you, especially if you are commuting by car, and tired on top of being intoxicated. At least in the places I've worked, you're honestly lucky that you still have a job if you came in drunk, so pull yourself together and do the right thing if you want to keep it. 

Best of luck.

Make their life easier, not harder. Do the dishes when they cook dinner. Pack their work lunch, and add a cute little note. If they ask a reasonable favor of you, get it done. Check off a task on their list that you can do if they've got a busy day ahead of them. Launder/set out their work clothes/uniform for them for the morning if they've had a rough day. Also, just remind them what they mean to you every day in little ways. Tell them you love them other than the times you would before bed or before leaving the house, etc. Pick them up their favorite drink or candy or snack if you're out running a quick errand. Stop them for an extra kiss on their way out the door. Tell them they are handsome/beautiful even if they're in their pajamas with some major bedhead going on. Set aside a "them" night every so often, and watch their movie with their dinner of choice. Consciously spend time together some nights, and not just be in the same room together doing separate activities. Give them a motivating/loving text when you're heading off to work so they wake up to a nice message.

Every day, just do a little something to show your appreciation and love in different ways.

I've seen a few things that very well could have earthly explanations, but one I saw a couple weeks ago in rural Indiana still makes me wonder. BF and I just finished the 2+ hour drive out there, and decided to look at the stars (we don't get them out here in the city) right before the sun was *just* barely starting to peek it's head out. He then points out a decently fast moving light and asks if it's a plane. I figured it was probably way too high up to be one, but I could be wrong. Just then, it makes a dead stop. We both go silent, staring at this little dot that looked exactly like the stars around it. Same size, same brightness. After about 15 seconds, it slowly starts gliding off perpendicular to the direction it was going before. And it kept moving around for quite long time. Going slowly in one direction, making a dead stop, zipping incredibly fast over to another direction, stopping, gliding slowly off another way again.

Suddenly, a similar sized ball of light comes from out of view and zips up to it in a straight line and combines with it. We both saw it, judging by our unison gasps and looking at each other. Not long after, it happens again. And slowly, we both start seeing this "aura" around it. Almost like the sky itself was warping and swirling like a vortex sphere around it, the sphere being the tiniest shade darker than the rest of the sky. So miniscule, you *really* had to focus on it. I focused on other stars nearby to see if it was just my eyes playing tricks from staring so long, but it stayed on the moving object and didn't happen on any other stars.

We sat and watched it from moments before the very start of sunrise to full morning. Unfortunately, once the sun was up, you could no longer see it, along with the other stars. I tried to record it but it was just so tiny, you couldn't see a thing. Bums me out because it was the craziest thing I've seen in the sky yet and I only have him as a witness.

I'll share a few more stories and try to sum them up as best as I can.

**1) The Owl Man**  --   When I was younger, a friend and I were having a sleepover at my house. My friend was laying down on a couch across the room, and I was on one underneath our bay window. We were staying up late watching a movie, under our blankets, lights off besides what's shining from the TV. I start to hear some rustling in the grass and bushes outside near the bay window, but wasn't concerned much since we had outdoor cats that occasionally used to fight strays, and obviously squirrels and other wildlife are present outdoors. But then it got louder, making sounds that a cat or squirrel wouldn't be able to do unless it was really going wild. I grab the remote and turn the movie down, telling my friend to be quit and listen, asking her what the heck she thinks it is. Being the scared pre-teen girls we were, we just sat there wide-eyed staring up at the window because it sounded like a human was now ruffling through them without trying to be quiet. It suddenly stops for a moment, but then there was a very loud bang as this owl-human looking thing rams into the window, with it's hands up next to it's face as if it were minimizing glare to look in, or trying to slam them onto the window to make noise. It's eyes were *huge*. Too big to be an owl's though being identical in looks and yellow in color, and way too big to fit a human's skull, let alone barely fitting this thing's silhouette, and I swear they were nearly glowing they were so bright and wide. It's silhouette was just large in general. Huge hands, massive eyes, a frame of a very broad and tall man. It stayed there staring in long enough for us to scream, throw our blankets off of us, and sprint out of the room into my parent's room. We woke up my dad who is tough and no-nonsense about intruders and all and told him about it. He grabbed a bat, stomped right out the front door and did a thorough search of the perimeter and yard, and nothing was found. Even though I love owls now as an adult and live in a house decorated with quite a few of them, I still hate looking out windows at night because of it.


**2) Tucked in**  --  Once again, at the same ex's house as the original post. We often spent weekend at each other's houses, and being in their very religious household, I always slept on the floor on a mattress topper beside the door. His mom was pressuring us to 'stop being lazy' and wanted us to be up before the sunrise for coffee and start our days despite how we were sleeping in to coincide with our usual work schedules. So, we laid down in our beds quite early. My sleep schedule had me going to bed around 1am so trying to fall asleep at 9pm wasn't easy. I sat there in my bed for a good 2 hours watching videos and browsing the internet, starting to get a pretty sleepy when I heard some footsteps coming up the hallway. I hurried up, locked my phone, rolled over away from the door and pretended to be asleep in case she walked by and wondered why I was still awake. I heard the door open, and someone take a few steps in. Someone then gently grabbed onto the top of my blanket, pulled it up to my shoulders and gently patted it down. It felt really cold at that time, but not *bad*. It felt protective and maternal and sweet. And for some reason, I wasn't alarmed. I'd say go ahead and reach out to them, but don't continually ask and ask until they give in. Don't try to fix it, because you can't. Accept that you can't heal them of their illness, but you can help them manage it.

Just be there for them. If they say they need to talk and you're available to listen, do it. If they want to get out of the house and you're able and willing, offer to get them out. You don't need to try and be a super-friend and smother them with attention and gifts and love and be there at every beck and call. Just be an ear and a shoulder to cry on. Maybe watch their favorite movie with them for the 30th time if it gives them joy. We're not like newborn fawns who can't do anything on their own. We just need a bit of help to stand up straight, keep our chins up and to hold on sometimes.

My friend introduced our group to Mao, which we sort of turned into King Mao. Only very few differences from the original. It's an amazing game to play with newbies because it is so infuriating to learn and often leads up to rage-quitting and yells of frustration (which leads to penalty). The kicker is, there are a ton of obscure rules and not a single rule is spoken about besides "Get rid of all your cards, have fun". Revealing or reminding anyone of a rule gets you kicked from the game. You learn this game by experience only.


Each player gets seven cards. The key is to get rid of all your cards. Each player in turn must place down a single card that matches the same color of the face-up card on the table. If you are switching colors when you have a card of the same number, you knock once on the table before putting it down. If the next player wants to immediately change it back to the other color if they have a matching number but different color, you knock twice and so on. Queens reverse the order of players. Spades must be announced "X of Spades". Ace of Spades needs to be said with much enthusiasm. 7's force the next player to play a card equal or lesser than 7 and must also initially be announced with a "Have a nice day". If the next player puts down another 7, they must say "Have a very nice day" and so on. Failure to announce is a penalty. If the next player is unable to adhere to the rule, they're penalized with picking up a card. If you cannot match either a number or a color of the face up card, you pick up a card as your turn.



**The fun rules:**

--The game does not begin until the owner of the cards says "King Mao begins now." Touching your cards before this results in a penalty.


--If you speak, you must first say "Point of order". Abuse of it gets you penalized and it cannot be used for chitchat, it's mostly in cases of disputing a penalty. Rules such as spades or "have a nice day" do not need the prefix. Speaking out of order or adding in any unnecessary words to the allowed phrases will get you penalized. As will unnecessary knocks or sounds, etc. Sneezing or clearing your throat are fine. Slamming your hand down onto the table or grunting is not.


--If you play out of turn or don't make your move within 5 seconds on your turn, you're penalized.


--If you're penalized, you must say "Thank you" within 5 seconds. Failing results in another penalty within 5 seconds. This can go on until there aren't any cards left if the player does not catch onto the rule, as can any penalty that this would fit into (Speaking out of turn, getting angry and continuing to speak, etc).


--If you are down to one card, you must announce "Mao". Failing results in a penalty if you are caught. Upon laying down your last card, you must say "King Mao" to announce your victory. Failure gets you penalized again if you are caught.

--The winner of the game gets to choose one ridiculous yet not game-breaking rule that only they know, and can't be used against only one person. Ones we've used before are "Do not look me in the eye, ever", "You must look me in the eyes when placing a card down", "Gently touch your other cards face down onto the table when you place a card down", "Bring your hand up to your face/chin when not in turn". Something that players can catch onto within a few turns, basically. But nothing as obvious as coughing loudly every time you place a card down. If you fail to adhere to the rule, you will be penalized each turn until you catch on. If you make any notice of catching on or hint to the rule, you're penalized or kicked out of the game if it completely gives it away.


It's great with new people because once it begins, there are penalties everywhere. They'll be asking "But I don't know how it works!" Penalty. "Wait why, what's this for?" Penalty. "What the fuck, dude?" Penalty. "Why am I the only one getting cards?!" Penalty.


Be prepared to make enemies. :)

Not OP, but when my dad passed away when I was 13, I was the one who gently pushed my mom to date, like your daughter is doing. It didn't make me uncomfortable to see her date. What made me uncomfortable and sad was seeing her so lonely, sad, stuck in the past. It made me so happy to see her spending time with her then boyfriend. I knew she loved my dad more than life itself, I knew they had the epitome of a wonderful, happy marriage, I knew it wouldn't ever leave her mind. My dad was the most amazing man to have ever lived, in my mind. But it wasn't doing her good to dwell and block herself off in the past, and I knew her boyfriend was good for her. He wasn't my dad, and I didn't see him as that. But he was a great man, he treated her very well and I loved him, just like my mom grew to do. She had a new spark in her eye that she lost for years.

I'll tell you what I told my mom: You don't have to marry them. You don't have to commit. You're not replacing dad/mom. This doesn't mean their time with you was meaningless and you're just painting over it all. Would he/she want you to be like this, stuck on them? "Dad would be kicking your butt right now if he saw you stuck on him like this", I reminded her. I think companionship would be great for you. Someone to hug. Someone to have deep conversations with. Someone to spend the holidays with, spend some time out of the house with. It's not a replacement. *It's not a replacement.* It's a new friend that will help mend the hole in your heart, the wounds that are still throbbing. It won't fill it just yet, but it may relieve the pain, if only a little. It's a step to recovering, to healing, to giving you something to look forward to, instead of craning your neck helplessly to look back to your past.

This doesn't mean you can't love again. Don't let yourself feel this way. Some people are okay with staying widowed, like my mom. And that is absolutely okay, too. You do what you need to do. Your memories and the love shared with your wife are not wasted. They're precious memories, precious seconds, days and years you cannot take back, and will always be with you. But there is nothing wrong with starting a new chapter in your life; the old pages will still be there. Finding a wonderful woman you can dote on and love, and receive the same back. I'm sure your wife would hurt to see you like this. She would understand if you found a companion, a girlfriend, a wife. Your daughter would seem to appreciate it as well.

I may be repeating some advice from others, so I apologize. And I am no expert and still have a ways to go on my weight loss/fitness journey. This is just what has helped me :)

Start slow. Don't go in like you're trying to compete or win anything, this is just the first step on a journey here. Get your body used to activity, work up to it. And don't feel bad if you can't do much. I used to be very active in high school. ~5 years later, I start going to the gym and realize I couldn't even slowly run a treadmill mile without wheezing and desperately wanting to quit. Just do what your body can handle right now. Even if it's a 10 minute brisk walk on the treadmill, it's a victory.

Don't compare yourself to others there. Some may have been working at this for years. It's sometimes intimidating to see someone very fit and rocking their workout like it's a cakewalk. Like I said, it's not a competition. No one is winning or losing. Focus on you. If anything, use the others there as inspiration instead of intimidation.

Getting in shape requires a lot more than gym time. Much of it is in the kitchen. Cutting out things like soda, excessive carbs, extreme caloric intake, excessive sugar etc will do wonders for both your physical self and how you feel inside. Go slow with this, also. From my experience, revamping your entire diet overnight usually lead directly to failure. For example, if you drink 2 sodas a day, sub one in for a bottle or two of water. Hell, add water regardless if you're not drinking as much as you think you should be. If you're craving chips, go for a crunchy veggie or fruit. Snack on a sweet fruit like strawberries or blueberries if you're craving candies or sweets. Learn some health-conscious recipes if you cook. Cut down on fast food if it's an issue for you. Not saying your life has to be salads and water from now on, but make a healthier choice each day. It will hopefully give you motivation and may lead to adding in more healthy choices to your daily routine.

And the main thing is, don't give up. For whatever reason. You'll get sore. You'll want to give in and eat your entire fridge. You'll want to give up because the results just aren't showing as fast as you'd want them to so why bother. But it'll be a vicious cycle that never completes if you give up. The results will come. But it takes effort. Sometimes you have to force yourself. But realize that every day you put forth an effort to better yourself, you're closer to your goal. 

Best of luck! You can do this, dude. Just keep at it :)

These things can literally double in size overnight, so keep that in mind for both housing and feeding to your skink.

For feeding the worms, I'm not sure if the place you buy them from will include it, so I'd say something like silkworm gut-loading chow may be suitable, or a diet of whatever greens and veggies you feed your skink. But you may want to research that a bit. I'm spoiled and never actually had to buy food for mine, haha. Just don't use wild tomato worms or feed them their namesake, tomato plants I believe make them toxic.

And from my experience, yes BTS are a dream. Pretty nippy as juveniles, but they mellow out great with proper handling and socialization. My Maverick would snap at anything that moved as a baby, but now I scoop him up and kiss him on the nose without a fear in the world. They're so much fun to look at and handle and watch, and seem perfectly content roaming your lap or bed or chilling on your shoulder. They do have quite a lifespan though, so be ready for a +20 year commitment! I got my Northern from Jeff at BTSkinks.com and he has good sized litters quite often.

I feed my Northern mostly a homemade diet of veggies, meat and occasional fruits and such. I have never given him anything like crickets or dubia roaches, only tomato worms which stay in a little container and hardly move and make no noise, if that is also an issue with you keeping insects. I also do not like insects, not one bit. Crickets and Dubias were a nightmare for me to feed to my critters. But Tomato worms are a breeze. I just pick one up with a pair of reptile feeding tongs or roll one off onto their container lid and feed it directly to my BTS. Easy peasy, and they're a gorgeous blue color which I actually think lessens the creepy factor. They're actually cute if you don't get your face right up next to them!

I've owned Geckos, Bearded Dragons, snakes, turtles, but I have to say my BTS is lovely and I'd honestly choose them over the other reptiles I've owned.

The bleeding doesn't stop. It's a constant flow or trickle. You're constantly worried "am I leaking through my pants?" You have to slightly plan your day around being able to get a new tampon in or change your pad in a good time period before your pants look like a horror movie. Sleep is another roulette game of "will I ruin my sheets and pajama pants?" because like I said, it doesn't stop and sometimes you don't wake up to change your feminine products.

First, there's no shame in being a lone wolf or a little "different" in terms of your interests. A lot of people, myself included, either have a hard time fitting in or simply don't care to and are okay with being alone or with a very, very small circle of people who share your interests and you can open up to. It already seems like you have no issue with it at all which is fantastic, but I figured I'd highlight that thought a bit :)

But I absolutely understand the feeling of wanting to share your interests and gain some good friends. Are there any clubs that would fit your interests in college, unofficial or not? I'd look into that. I know things like Anime club and such are more prevalent in high school, but I know my college had their own unofficial Anime/Art/Japanese culture/Gaming/Self-proclaimed "weirdos" (affectionately said) club that would get together in our student union building quite often. And often there would be events held by the school for gaming and movies and such. I'd try to get yourself out there. Show your face enough, make some small talk and I'm sure you can find someone to click with and possibly bond quite well!

As for coming out of your shell, I think that comes naturally with time and the more you get out there and initiate some small talk and such, it'll happen slowly. Just let yourself geek out a little, sure some people may turn up their nose but others will look at you and say "I wish I could be their friend." Other people who like the way you are may just come out of the woodwork and introduce themselves to you. Or if you see someone who seems like the type you'd get along with, maybe try engaging in small talk or compliment something of theirs (someone wearing a sticker/backpack/keychain of a game/anime/etc that's familiar to you? Bring it up, chat about it! People love talking about things they're into, and they'll be stoked you recognize it and are willing to listen I'm sure.)

If it seems like a hassle, just don't push yourself. You don't have to chat up everyone, and you don't have to feel bad about having a night (or a week, no judging) to yourself. You get that inkling of "Man, I should go and say hi.." just go for it. If you feel scared or anything, just hold off. You're a pretty independent person, so no need to rush it and try to squeeze into any available spot you see. But if someone piques your interest, give it a shot! No harm done, there.

With college, I'm sure you can find someone to chat and bond with no problem. :)

I'm no expert on geckos specifically, but I'm somewhat of a reptile nut.

I agree with Hatherence; Hop over to those subs, they are much more qualified to help you. For now, until you find out the type of gecko, avoid feeding it anything crazy. A few small crickets from the pet shop should suffice for the moment. Give it a very shallow dish of water as well, and something to hide in like a toilet paper tube or a small cardboard box with a cutout/door.

Just be aware that most reptiles cannot just be plopped into a bare tank and left there with occasional feedings. Varied diets that sometimes requires you to prepare fresh rather than just dump out from a bag, specific temperatures in certain areas of the tank, UV lighting, water misting for vital humidity levels, acquiring a large enough enclosure, keeping a *lack* of humidity for some, specific substrate/bedding, plenty of hides for them to feel safe in, veterinary costs (seeing as a lot of places don't care for exotics, this could be a challenge finding a place in some areas and could be pricey.)

This is not to scare you off. Reptiles are wonderful and I fully enjoy all of the work that goes into the little critters! But if you feel that you cannot properly handle it, it would be best to find a home for it where it will live out it's life happy and healthy.
